name: Uyghur Khaganate
summary: A Turkic steppe empire that overthrew the Göktürks in 744. It helped the Tang dynasty crush the An Lushan rebellion and adopted Manichaeism as its official religion.

location.value: The Mongolian Plateau, with its capital Ordu-Baliq on the Orkhon river.

terrain.value: Steppe and the Orkhon river valley in Mongolia.

climate.value: A harsh winter and famine (839) weakened the khaganate just before its fall.

resources.value: Horses, herds and control of trade.

urbanisation.value: Ordu-Baliq was a walled city, unusual for a steppe empire.

disease.value: A livestock epidemic just before the collapse.

migration.value: After 840 Uyghurs moved south-west to Gansu and the Turfan basin (Qocho).

economicBase.value: Herding and the horse-for-silk trade with Tang China.

tradeRoutes.value: Sold horses to Tang China for huge amounts of silk; Sogdian merchants traded along the Silk Road.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: Silk received from the Tang served as wealth.

inequality.value: A tribal confederation under the Uyghur nobility.

governmentType.value: A monarchy over a tribal confederation (the “Nine Tribes”, Toquz Oghuz).

keyRulers.value: Qutlugh Bilge Köl (744–747, founder), Bayanchur, Bögü Qaghan (adopted Manichaeism).

succession.value: Hereditary, with coups among the nobles.

institutions.value: Sogdian advisers helped run the state and trade.

eliteConflict.value: A rebellion among the nobles weakened the khagan.

armyAndTech.value: Cavalry that helped the Tang retake Chang’an and Luoyang (757).

majorWars.value: Helped suppress the An Lushan rebellion; destroyed by the Yenisei Kyrgyz in 840.

territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Uyghur Khaganate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Mackerras, The Uighur Empire (1972)

alliancesRivals.value: Ally of Tang China; rival of Tibet and the Kyrgyz.

scienceEducation.value: Manichaean and Buddhist texts translated into Old Uyghur.

openness.value: Open to Sogdian merchants and their religion.

religion.value: Manichaeism became the official religion; Tengrism, Buddhism and Nestorian Christianity also present.

languageWriting.value: Old Uyghur and Middle Chinese; Old Uyghur later used a script derived from Sogdian.

artsArchitecture.value: The walled city of Ordu-Baliq and the Karabalgasun inscription.

socialStructure.value: Royal clan, nobles, herders, Sogdian merchants.

sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Uyghur Khaganate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Mackerras, The Uighur Empire (1972)

neighbours.value: Tang China, the Tibetan Empire, the Yenisei Kyrgyz and the Karluks.

riseSignals.value: Overthrew the Second Turkic Khaganate in 744.

peakPeriod.value: Around 800, when it controlled the Mongolian steppe and Silk Road routes.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Uyghur Khaganate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Mackerras, The Uighur Empire (1972)

declineSignals.value: Famine, disease and internal revolt in the 830s.

outcome.value: Destroyed by the Yenisei Kyrgyz in 840; succeeded by the Kingdom of Qocho, the Gansu Uyghurs and the Kara-Khanids.

sources.value: Chinese records, inscriptions. Checked against Wikipedia (“Uyghur Khaganate”).

overallCertainty.value: Medium. Known mostly from Chinese records and a few inscriptions.

knownFor.label: Ordu-Baliq
knownFor.note: A walled capital city on the steppe.

knownFor.label: Horse-for-silk trade
knownFor.note: Uyghur horses were traded to Tang China for silk.

knownFor.label: Manichaean state religion
knownFor.note: One of the few states ever to adopt Manichaeism.
